notes: Near byte-identical to the original pre-strip implementation (same auth gate, same state check, same event). No functional difference found.
Correctly uses the real Marten Inline-snapshot config for Application (verified in ShelterAdoptionModule.cs) and the same shelter-ownership gate + IsOpen filter as the original.

Silently drops the original's await bus.ScheduleAsync(new CheckApplicationStale(...), 15 days) call entirely — no IMessageBus injected, nothing scheduled. Endpoint returns 200 and its own new tests pass, but the stale-application escalation flow (MarkApplicationStale/CloseStaleApplication) will never fire for real requests. failure_class: spec-misread (the scheduling requirement lived only in the deleted file's own doc comment, invisible after stripping) + weak-test-coverage (new tests never assert a message was scheduled).

Functionally identical to the original despite the cross-slice coupling confound (had to also recreate CheckApplicationStale, which RequestAdditionalDetails' original file depends on) — correctly reconstructed the idempotency re-check guard and the 30-day CheckApplicationClosed follow-up scheduling.
Functionally identical to the original — correct terminal-state guard (Stale-only, no further scheduling since Closed is terminal), same as ground truth.

Functionally identical to the original; correctly inferred the applicant-only (not Shelter-role) ownership gate from domain semantics alone, matching the original's own note about a board actor-label artifact.

Functionally equivalent to the original. Minor stylistic nit only: reads RejectionReason back off the aggregate with a null-forgiving "!" instead of reusing request.Reason directly — consistent with the codebase's established self-applying-aggregate pattern (other handlers rely on the same immediacy for Status), not a functional bug.

Drops the original's DogListing status cascade entirely — original calls dogListing.UpdateStatus(DogListingStatus.Adopted) via a writable event stream in the same SaveChangesAsync; rebuild only does a read-only LoadAsync to denormalize DogName. After "approving" an adoption, the dog's listing silently stays available, so other applicants could apply for an already-adopted dog. The new test file's own comment literally documents the (wrong) assumption: "DogListing (read-only, for the cascaded event's DogName)". More severe than the RequestAdditionalDetails miss — this breaks the core listing state machine, not just a background housekeeping trigger. failure_class: spec-misread (the v3 ENRICHMENT cascade requirement lived only in the deleted file's own doc comment, citing Spec/K9CRUSH.emlang.v3.yaml — not discoverable from the bare slice title or sibling RejectApplicationHandler, which explicitly does NOT do this cascade) + weak-test-coverage.
